Annotation Interface ChaosScenario

@Target({TYPE,METHOD}) @Retention(RUNTIME) @Inherited @Repeatable(ChaosScenarios.class) @Deprecated(since="2.0", forRemoval=true) public @interface ChaosScenario
Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
Use WithChaos: it takes the full plan JSON model (every selector, effect and policy field), works with every test extension, and is honoured by ChaosQuarkusExtension too. This annotation only knows a few selectors and effect shorthands and will be removed in 3.0.
Declarative chaos scenario activation for Quarkus tests.

When placed on a test class or method, the ChaosQuarkusExtension reads the annotation metadata, builds a matching ChaosScenario, and activates it on the class-scoped ChaosSession opened for the test.

Multiple @ChaosScenario annotations may be placed on the same element — each is activated independently. Test-method annotations take precedence for parity with the usual JUnit annotation-override rules.

Example

@QuarkusChaosTest
@ChaosScenario(id = "slow-jdbc", selector = "jdbc", effect = "delay:PT0.1S")
class OrderServiceTest {

  @Test
  @ChaosScenario(id = "slow-http", selector = "httpClient", effect = "delay:PT0.5S")
  void placesOrder() {
    // both the class-level slow-jdbc scenario and the method-level slow-http scenario
    // are active while this test runs.
  }
}

  • Element Details

    • id

      String id
      Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
      Unique identifier for this scenario; used in diagnostics and JFR events. Must be non-blank.
      Returns:
      the scenario identifier

    • selector

      String selector
      Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
      Selector identifier, one of "executor", "jvmRuntime", "httpClient", or "jdbc". A pair with effect() that cannot apply is refused with IllegalArgumentException before anything is activated.
      Returns:
      the selector identifier

    • effect

      String effect
      Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
      Effect identifier.

      Supported values:

      • "delay:<iso-duration>" — delay for the given ISO-8601 duration (e.g., "delay:PT0.1S" for 100 ms).
      • "suppress" — silently discard the matched operation: with "executor" the task submission only (a worker's task run cannot be skipped); refused for "httpClient" and "jdbc", whose calls cannot be skipped (use a delay).
      • "freeze" — shorthand for a clock-skew freeze effect (paired with "jvmRuntime").
      Returns:
      the effect identifier

    • scope

      String scope
      Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
      Scope of the scenario, matching ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope. Defaults to "JVM". JVM-scoped scenarios are activated at JVM scope via ChaosControlPlane.activate(ChaosScenario) and are tracked per-class or per-method for teardown in afterAll/afterTestExecution. SESSION-scoped scenarios are activated on the class-scoped ChaosSession and are torn down by session.close() in afterAll.
      Returns:
      the scenario scope name
      Default:
      "JVM"
